subject: general
question: In a circle with center O, two parallel chords GH and IJ are on opposite sides of the center. The length of chord GH is 24 cm and the length of chord IJ is 10 cm. If the distance between the two chords is 17 cm, what is the diameter of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Half-chord lengths are 24/2 = 12 cm and 10/2 = 5 cm.

Note that sum of half-chords (12 + 5) equals the distance between them (17 cm).

In such cases, the distance of chords from the center are these half-lengths: 5 cm and 12 cm.

Radius r = √(12² + 5²) = √169 = 13 cm.

Diameter = 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

**∴ Answer = 26 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Chord GH = 24 cm, Chord IJ = 10 cm, Distance between chords = 17 cm.

**Formula used:**

Radius² = (Half chord length)² + (Distance from center)²

 
• 
• O 
• G H I J 
• r x y x + y = 17 

**Calculations:**

Let the perpendicular distance from center O to chord GH be x and to IJ be y.

⇒ x + y = 17 (since chords are on opposite sides)

⇒ In right triangle with GH: r² = (24/2)² + x² = 144 + x²

⇒ In right triangle with IJ: r² = (10/2)² + y² = 25 + y²

⇒ 144 + x² = 25 + y²

⇒ y² − x² = 119

⇒ (y − x)(y + x) = 119

⇒ (y − x)(17) = 119 ⇒ y − x = 7

⇒ Solving x + y = 17 and y − x = 7 gives y = 12 and x = 5

⇒ r² = 144 + 5² = 169 ⇒ r = 13 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 13 = 26 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm, which is option (2).**
